summary:
Earth Information Jukebox is an interactive web-based prototype designed to make Earth science more accessible through sound and visual exploration.

The website allows users to explore environmental themes such as global temperature, ocean conditions, and Arctic ice. It presents interactive visualizations and generates sounds that change according to numerical data values. By combining visual information with audio, the project demonstrates how complex environmental concepts can be communicated through more than one sense.

The project is inspired by NASA's Earth Information Jukebox challenge, which encourages participants to transform Earth science visualizations into engaging sound experiences.

Our goal is to develop an educational platform that makes environmental information easier to explore and understand. The current prototype uses demonstration data and provides a foundation for future integration with real NASA Earth science datasets and visualizations.
details:
Project Overview

Earth Information Jukebox, also known as The Earth Sound Lab, is an interactive website prototype developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It explores how environmental information can be represented through both visualizations and sound.

How It Works

Users can explore three environmental themes: Global Temperature, Ocean Health, and Arctic Sea Ice. The website displays interactive charts, numerical values, and an animated Earth visualization.

Using the Web Audio API, the application generates sounds based on numerical data values. Changes in data influence the pitch and timing of the audio, allowing users to explore information through listening.

Users can also import their own CSV datasets to experiment with different numerical information.

Technologies Used

The website was developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. The Web Audio API provides sound generation, while GitHub Pages hosts the website.

Benefits and Impact

The project aims to make Earth science more engaging, interactive, and accessible. It demonstrates an alternative way to communicate complex environmental information by combining sight and sound.

Development Challenges

The main challenges involved designing an interactive interface, mapping numerical values to meaningful sounds, and maintaining compatibility across different screen sizes.

Current Limitations

The current prototype uses illustrative demonstration datasets rather than verified NASA measurements. NASA Earth Information Center visualizations and real Earth science datasets are intended for future integration.
